description: Get facts for a specific IoT Hub or all IoT Hubs.

parameters.name: ad_user
parameters.description: Active Directory username. Use when authenticating with an Active Directory user rather than service principal.

parameters.name: adfs_authority_url
parameters.description: Azure AD authority url. Use when authenticating with Username/password, and has your own ADFS authority.

parameters.name: api_profile
parameters.description: Selects an API profile to use when communicating with Azure services. Default value of latest is appropriate for public clouds; future values will allow use with Azure Stack. Default: "latest"

parameters.name: auth_source
parameters.description: Controls the source of the credentials to use for authentication. Can also be set via the ANSIBLE_AZURE_AUTH_SOURCE environment variable. When set to auto (the default) the precedence is module parameters -> env -> credential_file -> cli. When set to env, the credentials will be read from the environment variables When set to credential_file, it will read the profile from ~/.azure/credentials. When set to cli, the credentials will be sources from the Azure CLI profile. subscription_id or the environment variable AZURE_SUBSCRIPTION_ID can be used to identify the subscription ID if more than one is present otherwise the default az cli subscription is used. When set to msi, the host machine must be an azure resource with an enabled MSI extension. subscription_id or the environment variable AZURE_SUBSCRIPTION_ID can be used to identify the subscription ID if the resource is granted access to more than one subscription, otherwise the first subscription is chosen. The msi was added in Ansible 2.6. Choices: "auto" ← (default) "cli" "credential_file" "env" "msi"

parameters.name: cert_validation_mode
parameters.description: Controls the certificate validation behavior for Azure endpoints. By default, all modules will validate the server certificate, but when an HTTPS proxy is in use, or against Azure Stack, it may be necessary to disable this behavior by passing ignore. Can also be set via credential file profile or the AZURE_CERT_VALIDATION environment variable. Choices: "ignore" "validate"

parameters.name: client_id
parameters.description: Azure client ID. Use when authenticating with a Service Principal or Managed Identity (msi). Can also be set via the AZURE_CLIENT_ID environment variable.

parameters.name: cloud_environment
parameters.description: For cloud environments other than the US public cloud, the environment name (as defined by Azure Python SDK, eg, AzureChinaCloud, AzureUSGovernment), or a metadata discovery endpoint URL (required for Azure Stack). Can also be set via credential file profile or the AZURE_CLOUD_ENVIRONMENT environment variable. Default: "AzureCloud"

parameters.name: disable_instance_discovery
parameters.description: Determines whether or not instance discovery is performed when attempting to authenticate. Setting this to true will completely disable both instance discovery and authority validation. This functionality is intended for use in scenarios where the metadata endpoint cannot be reached such as in private clouds or Azure Stack. The process of instance discovery entails retrieving authority metadata from https://login.microsoft.com/ to validate the authority. By setting this to **True**, the validation of the authority is disabled. As a result, it is crucial to ensure that the configured authority host is valid and trustworthy. Set via credential file profile or the AZURE_DISABLE_INSTANCE_DISCOVERY environment variable. Choices: false ← (default) true

parameters.name: list_consumer_groups
parameters.description: List the consumer group of the built-in event hub. Choices: false true

parameters.name: list_keys
parameters.description: List the keys of IoT Hub. Note this will have network overhead for each IoT Hub. Choices: false true

parameters.name: log_mode
parameters.description: Parent argument.

parameters.name: log_path
parameters.description: Parent argument.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Limit results to a specific resource group.

parameters.name: password
parameters.description: Active Directory user password. Use when authenticating with an Active Directory user rather than service principal.

parameters.name: profile
parameters.description: Security profile found in ~/.azure/credentials file.

parameters.name: resource_group
parameters.description: The resource group to search for the desired IoT Hub.

parameters.name: secret
parameters.description: Azure client secret. Use when authenticating with a Service Principal.

parameters.name: show_endpoint_health
parameters.description: Get the health for routing endpoints. Note this will have network overhead for each IoT Hub. Choices: false true

parameters.name: show_quota_metrics
parameters.description: Get the quota metrics for an IoT hub. Note this will have network overhead for each IoT Hub. Choices: false true

parameters.name: show_stats
parameters.description: Show the statistics for IoT Hub. Note this will have network overhead for each IoT Hub. Choices: false true

parameters.name: subscription_id
parameters.description: Your Azure subscription Id.

parameters.name: tags
parameters.description: Limit results by providing a list of tags. Format tags as ‘key’ or ‘key:value’.

parameters.name: tenant
parameters.description: Azure tenant ID. Use when authenticating with a Service Principal.

parameters.name: test_route_message
parameters.description: Test routes message. It will be used to test all routes.

parameters.name: thumbprint
parameters.description: The thumbprint of the private key specified in x509_certificate_path. Use when authenticating with a Service Principal. Required if x509_certificate_path is defined.

parameters.name: x509_certificate_path
parameters.description: Path to the X509 certificate used to create the service principal in PEM format. The certificate must be appended to the private key. Use when authenticating with a Service Principal.

examples:
- name: Get facts for one IoT Hub
  azure_rm_iothub_info:
    name: Testing
    resource_group: myResourceGroup

- name: Get facts for all IoT Hubs
  azure_rm_iothub_info:

- name: Get facts for all IoT Hubs in a specific resource group
  azure_rm_iothub_info:
    resource_group: myResourceGroup

- name: Get facts by tags
  azure_rm_iothub_info:
    tags:
      - testing

return_values.name: azure_iothubs
return_values.description: List of IoT Hub dicts. Returned: always

return_values.name: cloud_to_device
return_values.description: Cloud to device message properties. Returned: always

return_values.name: max_delivery_count
return_values.description: The number of times the IoT hub attempts to deliver a message on the feedback queue. See https://docs.microsoft.com/azure/iot-hub/iot-hub-devguide-messaging#cloud-to-device-messages. Returned: always Sample: 10

return_values.name: ttl_as_iso8601
return_values.description: The period of time for which a message is available to consume before it is expired by the IoT hub. See https://docs.microsoft.com/azure/iot-hub/iot-hub-devguide-messaging#cloud-to-device-messages. Returned: always Sample: "1:00:00"

return_values.name: enable_file_upload_notifications
return_values.description: Whether file upload notifications are enabled. Returned: always Sample: "True"

return_values.name: event_endpoints
return_values.description: Built-in endpoint where to deliver device message. Returned: always

return_values.name: endpoint
return_values.description: The Event Hub-compatible endpoint. Returned: always Sample: "sb://iothub-ns-testing-1478811-9bbc4a15f0.servicebus.windows.net/"

return_values.name: partition_count
return_values.description: The number of partitions for receiving device-to-cloud messages in the Event Hub-compatible endpoint. See https://docs.microsoft.com/azure/iot-hub/iot-hub-devguide-messaging#device-to-cloud-messages. Returned: always Sample: 2

return_values.name: partition_ids
return_values.description: List of the partition id for the event endpoint. Returned: always Sample: ["0", "1"]

return_values.name: retention_time_in_days
return_values.description: The retention time for device-to-cloud messages in days. See https://docs.microsoft.com/azure/iot-hub/iot-hub-devguide-messaging#device-to-cloud-messages. Returned: always Sample: 1

return_values.name: host_name
return_values.description: Host of the IoT hub. Returned: always Sample: "testing.azure-devices.net"

return_values.name: id
return_values.description: Resource ID of the IoT hub. Returned: always Sample: "/subscriptions/XXXXXXXX-XXXX-XXXX-XXXX-XXXXXXXXXXXX/resourceGroups/myResourceGroup/providers/Microsoft.Devices/IotHubs/Testing"

return_values.name: identity
return_values.description: Identity for the Server. Returned: when available

return_values.name: type
return_values.description: Type of the managed identity Returned: always Sample: "UserAssigned"

return_values.name: user_assigned_identities
return_values.description: User Assigned Managed Identities and its options Returned: always

return_values.name: ip_filters
return_values.description: Configure rules for rejecting or accepting traffic from specific IPv4 addresses. Returned: always

return_values.name: action
return_values.description: The desired action for requests captured by this rule. Returned: always Sample: "Reject"

return_values.name: ip_mask
return_values.description: A string that contains the IP address range in CIDR notation for the rule. Returned: always Sample: "40.54.7.3"

return_values.name: name
return_values.description: Name of the filter. Returned: always Sample: "filter"

return_values.name: location
return_values.description: Location of the IoT hub. Returned: always Sample: "eastus"

return_values.name: resource_group
return_values.description: Resource group of the IoT hub. Returned: always Sample: "myResourceGroup."

return_values.name: routes
return_values.description: Route device-to-cloud messages to service-facing endpoints. Returned: always

return_values.name: condition
return_values.description: The query expression for the routing query that is run against the message application properties, system properties, message body, device twin tags, and device twin properties to determine if it is a match for the endpoint. For more information about constructing a query, see https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/iot-hub/iot-hub-devguide-routing-query-syntax Returned: always Sample: true

return_values.name: enabled
return_values.description: Whether to enable the route. Returned: always Sample: true

return_values.name: endpoint_name
return_values.description: The name of the endpoint in routing_endpoints where IoT Hub sends messages that match the query. Returned: always Sample: "foo"

return_values.name: source
return_values.description: The origin of the data stream to be acted upon. Returned: always Sample: "device_messages"

return_values.name: routing_endpoints
return_values.description: Custom endpoints. Returned: always

return_values.name: event_hubs
return_values.description: List of custom endpoints of event hubs. Returned: always

return_values.name: connection_string
return_values.description: Connection string of the custom endpoint. Returned: always Sample: "Endpoint=sb://quux.servicebus.windows.net:5671/;SharedAccessKeyName=qux;SharedAccessKey=****;EntityPath=foo"

return_values.name: subscription
return_values.description: Subscription ID of the endpoint. Returned: always Sample: "XXXXXXXX-XXXX-XXXX-XXXX-XXXXXXXXXXXX"

return_values.name: service_bus_queues
return_values.description: List of custom endpoints of service bus queue. Returned: always

return_values.name: service_bus_topics
return_values.description: List of custom endpoints of service bus topic. Returned: always

return_values.name: storage_containers
return_values.description: List of custom endpoints of storage. Returned: always

return_values.name: sku
return_values.description: Pricing tier for Azure IoT Hub. Returned: always Sample: "f1"

return_values.name: tags
return_values.description: Limit results by providing a list of tags. Format tags as ‘key’ or ‘key:value’. Returned: always Sample: {"key1": "value1"}

return_values.name: unit
return_values.description: Units in the IoT Hub. Returned: always Sample: 1
